title: One River, Several Places
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の史料、調査、システムの実証結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A river may appear on a map as a single continuous line, but its physical characteristics can differ considerably from one location to another.
sentences.ja: 川は地図上で一続きの線に見えるが、その物理的特性は場所によってかなり異なる。

sentences.en: The movement of water connects these locations, and conditions in one part of a river can influence conditions in another.
sentences.ja: 水の流れは場所同士を結び、川の一部の条件は別の場所の条件に影響し得る。

sentences.en: A description of an individual location may therefore provide an incomplete picture of the processes that shape the river as a whole.
sentences.ja: したがって個別地点の記述は川全体を形作る過程の不完全な像しか提供しないかもしれない。

sentences.en: This is important when people attempt to understand how changes in land use might affect a shared water environment.
sentences.ja: 土地利用の変化が共有の水環境にどう影響するか理解しようとするとき重要な点だ。

sentences.en: Imagine three groups of students observing different sections of a river for a school project.
sentences.ja: 学校活動のため川の異なる区間を観察する三班を想像しよう。

sentences.en: The first group examines a section near a field, the second visits an area beside a road, and the third studies a quieter location farther downstream.
sentences.ja: 第一班は畑の近くの区間、第二班は道路そば、第三班はさらに下流の静かな場所を調べる。

sentences.en: Each group records the appearance of the water and information about the surrounding land at the time of its visit.
sentences.ja: 各班は訪問時の水の外見と周囲の土地の情報を記録する。

sentences.en: Their teacher asks them to avoid treating these observations as a complete assessment of the environmental health of the river.
sentences.ja: 教師はこれらの観察を川の環境健全性の完全評価と扱わないよう求める。

sentences.en: When the students compare their records, they notice that the visits took place on different days and under different weather conditions.
sentences.ja: 記録を比較すると訪問が異なる日・天候条件下で行われたと気づく。

sentences.en: A difference between observations could therefore reflect a change over time rather than a difference associated with location.
sentences.ja: したがって観察差は場所に伴う違いでなく時間変化を反映している可能性がある。

sentences.en: The groups consider arranging further visits under more comparable conditions and recording additional information that might help explain the differences.
sentences.ja: より比較可能な条件で追加訪問を手配し、違いを説明する助けになる追加情報を記録することを考える。

sentences.en: They also examine a map showing how water moves between the locations they have visited.
sentences.ja: 訪れた地点間を水がどう移動するか示す地図も調べる。

sentences.en: The class recognizes that even observations collected on the same day would not necessarily establish the causes of the differences between locations.
sentences.ja: 同日に集めた観察でさえ場所間の違いの原因を必ずしも確定しないとクラスは認識する。

sentences.en: A real investigation of water quality would require suitable methods, appropriate measurements and an understanding of local circumstances.
sentences.ja: 実際の水質調査には適切な方法、測定値、現地事情の理解が必要となる。

sentences.en: The imagined project instead illustrates how the scale and timing of observations can affect the questions they are able to answer.
sentences.ja: 仮想活動は代わりに観察の規模と時期が回答できる問いにどう影響するかを示す。

sentences.en: The students learn to connect what they notice at each site with questions about processes occurring elsewhere.
sentences.ja: 各地点で気づいたことを別の場所で起きる過程についての問いと結びつけることを学ぶ。

sentences.en: Environmental understanding involves more than collecting separate descriptions of natural features.
sentences.ja: 環境理解には自然特徴の個別記述を集める以上のことが伴う。

sentences.en: It requires examining the connections through which changes in one place may become relevant to people and organisms in another.
sentences.ja: 一地点の変化が別地点の人や生物に関係し得るつながりを調べる必要がある。

sentences.en: A map of a river can serve as a reminder that the boundaries of an investigation are not necessarily the boundaries of the processes being investigated.
sentences.ja: 川の地図は調査の境界が調査対象過程の境界とは限らないことを思い出させる。

sentences.en: One river invites many observations, but their greatest value may lie in the relationships between them.
sentences.ja: 一つの川は多くの観察を促すが最大の価値は観察間の関係にあるかもしれない。

vocabulary.definition: in a way that must occur

questions.prompt: Why may a map's single line be misleading?
options: Every location has identical physical features.
The map shows that water never moves between locations.
The river has differing local conditions linked by water movement.
A river cannot be examined at different scales.
questions.explanation_ja: 場所の多様性とつながり。

options: Water appearance and surrounding land at its visit.
The complete chemical composition of all water.
The causes of every change in the river.

questions.prompt: Which location is examined by the third group?
options: A field beside the first site.
They establish that every observation is wrong.
They eliminate all variation between sites.
A difference may reflect time rather than location.
They show no further observation is necessary.
questions.explanation_ja: 時間と場所の影響の区別。

questions.prompt: Why examine the map of water movement?
options: It helps reveal relationships among the sites.
It establishes all causes of water pollution.
It replaces the need to record conditions.
It proves the sites were visited on the same day.

questions.prompt: What would a real assessment require?
options: A fixed explanation for every river.
Appropriate methods, measurements and local knowledge.

questions.prompt: Why would same-day visits not establish causes by themselves?
options: Same-day observations provide no information at all.
Comparable timing does not eliminate every other possible factor.
Every location must have exactly the same conditions.
Causes can be identified only from a map.
questions.explanation_ja: 条件をそろえても因果は未確定。

options: A river should be understood solely through its appearance.
All differences in observations are caused by weather.
River observations are more informative when interpreted through temporal and spatial relationships.
One location always represents the whole river.

grammar.explanation_ja: from A to Bで場所の違い。

grammar.focus: at the time of its visit
grammar.explanation_ja: at the time ofは〜の時点。

grammar.focus: rather than a difference associated with location

paraphrases.source: A river may appear on a map as a single continuous line, but its physical characteristics can differ considerably from one location to another.
paraphrases.rewrite: Different sections of a river may have substantially different physical features.

paraphrases.source: Each group records the appearance of the water and information about the surrounding land at the time of its visit.
paraphrases.rewrite: Each group notes surrounding conditions when it observes its site.

paraphrases.source: A difference between observations could therefore reflect a change over time rather than a difference associated with location.
paraphrases.rewrite: The differing records may be caused by changes over time instead of site differences.

paraphrases.source: A map of a river can serve as a reminder that the boundaries of an investigation are not necessarily the boundaries of the processes being investigated.
paraphrases.rewrite: A study's geographic limits may not match the limits of the natural processes.

discourse.role_ja: 地図上の単純さと現実の違い。
